images.title: What one small mark stands for
images.purpose: Show how to find the weight of one small mark (500 g shared into 10 gaps is 50 g) and read the needle on that scale.
images.composition: One large round scale with a 2 kg full turn, a note about the gaps at the top right, and the reading in a box below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. DIAL: a circle centred at (728, 380), radius 250 px, outline 8 px dark #1F2937, filled white. Hub: a circle of radius 16 px at the centre filled teal #0072B2. MARKS: exactly 40 small radial marks, one every 9 degrees clockwise from the top, mark 0 at the top. The 4 long marks (44 px long, 6 px thick, dark #1F2937) are marks 0, 10, 20, 30; every other mark is short (24 px long, 3 px thick, grey #6B7280). The marks run inward from radius 242. LABELS (centred on the point, 36 px, bold; the 0 is reddish purple #CC79A7, all others dark #1F2937): 0 at (728, 208); 500 g at (900, 380); 1 kg at (728, 552); 1 kg 500 g at (556, 380). NEEDLE: one straight needle from the hub to (635, 197), which is on mark 37 (333 degrees clockwise from the top), 9 px thick, amber #E69F00, ending in a small triangle arrowhead 26 px long; nothing else crosses it. READING BOX at the bottom centre, a rounded rectangle 560 by 80 px at x 448 to 1008, y 690 to 770, outline teal #0072B2, containing the text 1 kg 850 g (44 px, bold, dark). GAP NOTE at the top right, a rounded rectangle 400 by 130 px at x 1000 to 1400, y 60 to 190 with a 3 px outline #6B7280 and the two lines 500 g between labels, 10 gaps (32 px, dark) and 500 ÷ 10 = 50 g (36 px, bold, teal #0072B2). COUNT MARKS: on the arc between the 1 kg 500 g label (mark 30) and the needle (mark 37), seven small teal #0072B2 dots (12 px) sit on marks 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36 and 37, with the small text 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (28 px, teal) just outside the dial next to each dot. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of marks that differs from 40 (10 gaps between each pair of labels)
a needle that is not on mark 37, or more than one needle
any label other than 0, 500 g, 1 kg and 1 kg 500 g on the face
images.takeaway: One mark is the weight between two labels divided by the number of gaps: 500 ÷ 10 = 50 g, so the needle reads 1,500 g + 7 × 50 g = 1,850 g, which is 1 kg 850 g.
images.description: A round scale with a 2 kg full turn, 10 gaps between labels, and the needle on the 7th mark after 1 kg 500 g, reading 1 kg 850 g.
images.context: Concept image for What Does One Small Mark Stand For? It follows the idea of the scales in your maths book and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the gaps between two labels before reading the needle. The slip to watch: taking every mark to be 1 g.

image_decisions.why: The note and the counted marks show that the value of one mark comes first, then the reading.
